title: Power BI DAX with AI: From Prompt to Formula in Seconds
summary: An unvetted third-party blog walks through using Power BI's Copilot-based DAX assistant across three surfaces (Desktop query view, model view, and web modeling), with worked prompt examples for common measure patterns and a rundown of documented request/character limits and known blind spots.
audience: Power BI report/model authors who want a practical starting point for prompting Copilot to draft or refactor DAX measures, and who need to know where the assistant's model-visibility limits will bite.
why_it_matters: Prompt phrasing measurably changes DAX output quality (e.g. whether blank-safe guards are included), and the assistant's blind spots around new functions and Import-mode data sampling are the kind of gotchas that cause silent correctness bugs if authors assume Copilot sees full data or the latest DAX surface area.
takeaways: Copilot-assisted DAX authoring exists across at least three surfaces: an inline query-view assistant in Desktop, suggested/described measures at the model level, and a newer web-based modeling flow.
Explicit prompt qualifiers (e.g. asking for 'blank-safe' logic) materially change whether generated DAX includes defensive guards like BLANK()/ISBLANK() checks.

The assistant's visibility into Import-mode data is limited to sampled min/max values per column rather than full data distributions, which caps how well it can validate generated logic against real data shapes.
Newly released DAX functions can lag behind the assistant's own training/recognition, so very recent language features may not be reliably suggested or understood for a period after release.
Per Microsoft's own documentation, Copilot requires paid Fabric/Premium capacity — it is not available on trial capacity or Pro alone.

claims.text: A Copilot-based assistant is available inline in Power BI Desktop's DAX query view, invoked via a keyboard shortcut, to draft or edit DAX expressions from natural-language prompts.
Beyond the query-view assistant, Copilot can proactively suggest new measures based on existing model structure and can auto-generate plain-language descriptions of existing DAX measures.

Including an explicit qualifier such as 'blank-safe' in a DAX generation prompt is a practitioner pattern for reliably getting BLANK()/ISBLANK()-guarded logic in generated time-intelligence measures, rather than a version without such guards.

Common prompt-to-DAX patterns demonstrated include year-over-year growth using DATEADD with IF/ISBLANK protection, Top-N ranking using RANKX, and rolling averages using DATESINPERIOD combined with AVERAGEX.

For Import-mode semantic models, the DAX assistant's visibility into underlying data is limited to sampled minimum/maximum values per column rather than the full value distribution, which constrains how well generated logic can be validated against actual data shape.

Newly released DAX functions may not be reliably recognized or suggested by the Copilot DAX assistant for a period of time after their release, so authors should not assume immediate assistant support for brand-new DAX syntax.
Per Microsoft's documentation, Copilot for Power BI requires a paid Fabric or Power BI Premium capacity and is not supported on trial capacities, free SKUs, or a Pro license alone.
Per Microsoft's documentation, Copilot for Power BI supports prompts up to 10,000 characters across its Copilot surfaces.
Per Microsoft's documentation, Copilot for Power BI is not supported in sovereign cloud environments due to GPU availability constraints.
